fields.meta_title: Parent Consent Form Builder for Schools and Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a parent consent form families sign on a phone, with the dates it covers and the medical details staff check. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Parent Consent Form Staff Can Check on the Spot
fields.hero_description: Tell Emergent what the consent covers and who signs it. It builds a parent consent form families fill on a phone, plus the roster staff open before a child takes part.
fields.features_heading: What a Parent Consent Form Has to Settle
fields.features_subheading: Staff open these forms when they need an answer fast: a coach at the pool, a nurse with a sick student at the door.
fields.feature_1:
The child and what they may do

Ask for the child's name and date of birth, then the parent or guardian signing and how they are related. Name the activity and its dates. The form then records one clear decision.
fields.feature_2:
Consent with a start and an end

Set the dates a consent covers, such as one away meet or one school year. A form past its end date shows as expired on the roster, and the parent gets a link to sign again.
fields.feature_3:
Other adults a parent trusts

Let a parent list the grandparent or nanny who may pick the child up or bring them to a visit. Staff check a name against that list before the child leaves with any adult.
fields.feature_4:
Medical details staff can act on

Collect allergies and current medicines in their own fields, with a yes or no on emergency care if no parent answers the phone. The nurse or coach reads those answers first.
fields.feature_5:
Both parents, when the activity needs it

Send a second link to the other parent when an activity calls for two signatures. The form stays pending until both have signed, and each signature is saved with its own timestamp.
fields.feature_6:
Source code your team can keep

Export the full source of the consent form and its records to your GitHub. A district or league developer can host it on its own servers or connect it to a system already in use.

fields.tab_content_1:
Consent that ends when the meet does

Harbor Swim Club drives 14 swimmers to the Lakeside Invitational. Each parent's form names that meet and the adult their child rides with. The coach's roster pairs every swimmer with a driver. When the meet ends on Sunday, each consent closes, and the next away meet needs new signatures.
fields.tab_content_2:
Adults named by a parent, matched at the front desk

Parents at Maple Pediatrics list up to 3 other adults who may bring their child in and give consent to routine care. When a grandmother checks in 6-year-old Leo, the front desk sees her name on his list. An adult who is not on it waits while staff call a parent.
fields.tab_content_3:
The student applies and a parent finishes

High school juniors apply to a summer course at Ridgeview College and enter a parent's email. That parent gets a link to the form with the course and class times already filled in. Registration holds every student under 18 until a parent signs. This week, 9 of 52 applicants are waiting.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each service a parent allowed, on the nurse's screen

At Lincoln Middle's health center, the parent form lists 5 services, each with its own box. Ana's mother ticked 3 of them, sick visits included. When Ana walks in with a sore throat, the nurse sees those 3 ticks before the visit starts. Every form renews in August for the new school year.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Parent Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Settle what the parent is agreeing to, and for how long, before you write a single field.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Identify the child and the signer
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give the consent an end date
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write one sentence that says what the parent allows, such as riding to an away meet with another family or routine care at a school clinic. Every field on the form supports that sentence. Anything outside it belongs on a separate form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect the child's legal name and birthday. Ask how the signer is related to the child, and add a phone number that works on the day itself. A guardian who is not a parent can upload the court order that names them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set when the consent starts and when it stops, whether that is one weekend or one school year. Staff can then tell at a glance if it still applies, and a parent never wonders what a form signed two years ago still allows.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Include only what a coach or nurse would act on during the activity. A question nobody reads on the day is one more reason a parent stops halfway through. Put the doctor's phone number where staff can find it fast.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your wording into the prompt, then say who signs and when the consent ends. Emergent builds the form and the roster staff check, with a signature field at the bottom. Change any question later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick who gets an email or a Slack message when a parent signs, and who can open the medical fields. Every parent receives a PDF copy of the signed form showing the dates it covers, ready for the day they need to check it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form on a phone as a made-up family, sign it, then open the roster as staff. When a school or league supplies required wording, copy it exactly. Have a lawyer read any form that also waives rights.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is almost all issuer PDFs: a swim team's competition travel consent, Virginia's immunization registry text, a school district's medical authorization, a college program's under-18 form, a minor travel PDF on pdfFiller and a Minnesota special education model form. Jotform's field trip template is the only builder. Each PDF covers one program and ends at a signature on paper. This page explains what a parent consent form has to name (the child, the adult who signs, the activity and the dates the consent covers), answers the notarization and travel questions plainly, then shows the form as an app staff can check at the moment they need it: the coach at the pool, the front desk at a pediatric office, the registrar of a college course, the nurse in a school health center.
